items.q: Why does Beato prioritize relative pitch over perfect pitch?
items.a: He treats **ear training as learnable** — kids can pick up **relative pitch** fast (his son Dylan via the "Hey Joe" pentatonic pattern in minutes). **Beato Ear Training** teaches interval recognition, not innate perfect pitch, because working musicians need to hear relationships in real time.

items.q: What makes a guitarist's sound instantly recognizable?
items.a: **Guitar tone identity** is the test: great players are known by **one-note vibrato** alone. Solos work like speech — Hendrix, Gilmour, Knopfler use melodic flow, space, and silence (Miles Davis parallel). **Speed is not greatness.**

items.q: How good is AI music in Beato's experience?
items.a: On Suno/Udio, roughly **130 prompts → ~3 good songs**. Great songwriters benefit because they **recognize quality**; lyrics still lack edge. Beato finds AI generation **"boring, boring, boring"** and says kids spot reverb artifacts instantly — so he uses AI mainly for demo videos.

items.q: Why does he think authenticity will become more valuable?
items.a: AI excels at **overproduction**, so civilization will crave **raw talent**, long-form conversation, and real B.B. King over AI B.B. King. **"We humans want authenticity."** Cleanup ML (iZotope RX-style) is fine; macro generation as original art is not.

items.q: What's wrong with modern pop songwriting credits?
items.a: Hits often list **10–11 writers**, with **interpolations** recycling older songs (e.g. "Anxiety" tracing to Gotye → Luiz Bonfá 1967). Beato contrasts factory credits with **Taylor Swift / Billie Eilish / Bruno Mars** as counterexamples of real musicianship.

items.q: How did Beato survive Content ID warfare?
items.a: Early YouTube music clips meant **instant blocks** or **demonetization** (even a 20-second clip could send all revenue to the label). After a Rick Rubin episode, his lawyer fought **~4,000 claims and won all**. Labels shifted from blocking to monetizing after moments like Fleetwood Mac's TikTok "Dreams" surge.

items.q: What tradeoff does Spotify create for listening culture?
items.a: Streaming is a **faucet of access** plus algorithm discovery, but it **commoditizes albums**, weakens the listening ritual, and **underpays artists**. Beato still keeps **2005 iTunes WAV rips** for interview prep because listeners notice quality vs remastered streams.

items.q: What does Beato's career say about chasing fame early?
items.a: His channel took off at **55+** after decades of classical bass, jazz guitar master's work, college teaching, publishing, and producing — **music mastery before fame**. Signature advice: **"Somebody's gotta be successful, so why can't it be you?"** plus never waste a friendship.

items.q: How does he think about gear as craft?
items.a: He keeps **~100 real amps**, each doing **one thing really well** — if it doesn't, it goes. Pro Tools/Logic/Ableton plus Neural DSP/Kemper/Helix for travel, and a signature Gibson Les Paul Special, all in service of tone craft rather than collector clutter.
